books.title: Women in Love
books.author: D. H. Lawrence
books.desc: Two sisters in a Midlands mining town, a teacher and an artist, enter into passionate and troubled relationships with two very different men.
about: Ursula and Gudrun Brangwen are sisters living in the Erewash Valley on the borders of Nottinghamshire and Derbyshire in the 1910s; Ursula is a schoolteacher, Gudrun a painter. They become friends with two men: Rupert Birkin, a school inspector and restless intellectual, and Gerald Crich, heir to the local coal mines. As Ursula and Birkin search for a new kind of love, Gudrun is drawn into a destructive relationship with Gerald, while an intense attraction grows between the two men.
A sequel to The Rainbow, Lawrence's novel explores love, sexuality, industrial society, art and death, through long dialogues and charged symbolic scenes.

Women in Love was published in 1920. The character of Ursula draws on Lawrence's wife Frieda, Gudrun on Katherine Mansfield, Birkin partly on Lawrence himself and Gerald partly on John Middleton Murry.

books.title: Night and Day
books.author: Virginia Woolf
books.desc: In Edwardian London, the daughter of a distinguished literary family and a young suffrage worker face very different choices about love and work.
about: Katharine Hilbery, granddaughter of a famous poet, helps her mother write his biography in their elegant house in Cheyne Walk, Chelsea, while secretly studying mathematics. She becomes engaged to the poet William Rodney, without loving him. Ralph Denham, a young lawyer from a modest family, falls in love with her, while he is himself loved by Mary Datchet, who works for a women's suffrage society. Katharine's cousin Cassandra soon complicates matters further.

Woolf's second novel examines the relationships between love, marriage, happiness and work, and contrasts the lives of two women in a changing society. It contains many references to Shakespeare, especially As You Like It.

Night and Day was first published on 24 October 1919. Woolf began writing it in 1916 and, recovering from a nervous breakdown, was allowed to write only for a limited time each day. It is dedicated to her sister, Vanessa Bell.

books.title: The Beautiful and Damned
books.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
books.desc: A handsome idler waiting to inherit his grandfather's fortune and his beautiful wife Gloria drift through the parties of New York's café society.
about: Anthony Patch, a cultivated young man of leisure in New York, expects to inherit the fortune of his grandfather Adam Patch, a stern reformer. He falls in love with the beautiful and capricious Gloria Gilbert, and after their marriage the couple spend their time and money on parties with friends such as Maury Noble, while the film producer Bloeckman courts Gloria. As the years pass, their extravagance, idleness and drinking lead them towards ruin.

Fitzgerald's second novel is a realistic and pessimistic portrait of the American idle rich in the 1910s and the dawn of the Jazz Age. Anthony and Gloria were loosely modelled on Fitzgerald himself and his wife Zelda.
The Beautiful and Damned was serialised in Metropolitan magazine in late 1921 and published by Scribner's in March 1922.

books.title: His Last Bow
books.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
books.desc: Sherlock Holmes's later cases, ending on the eve of the First World War as he comes out of retirement to trap a German spy.
about: In a short preface, Dr Watson assures readers that Holmes is still alive, retired to a small farm on the Downs near Eastbourne, dividing his time between philosophy and agriculture. The stories that follow include "Wisteria Lodge", "The Bruce-Partington Plans", about stolen submarine plans, "The Devil's Foot", set in Cornwall, "The Red Circle", "The Disappearance of Lady Frances Carfax" and "The Dying Detective". In the title story, set in August 1914, Holmes returns to action to outwit the German agent Von Bork.
The collection shows Holmes and Watson in their later years, from Victorian London to the eve of the Great War.

His Last Bow: Some Reminiscences of Sherlock Holmes was published by John Murray in October 1917. Most of its stories had appeared in The Strand Magazine between 1908 and 1913, and the title story in Collier's in September 1917.

books.title: The Iron Heel
books.author: Jack London
books.desc: A manuscript found centuries later tells of the rise of a ruthless oligarchy in the United States and the socialist revolt against it.
about: The story is told by Avis Everhard, daughter of the physicist John Cunningham, in a manuscript discovered seven centuries later and annotated by a scholar of the future, Anthony Meredith. Avis describes how she met the socialist leader Ernest Everhard, who claimed that the whole social system rested on the exploitation of labour. Investigating the conditions of workers, she comes to share his views. Between 1912 and 1932, the great capitalists form an Oligarchy, the Iron Heel, which crushes all opposition.

London's dystopian novel combines political argument, a love story and visions of violent repression and revolt. Meredith's notes, written from a distant future, reveal from the start that the heroes' hopes will not be fulfilled in their lifetime.
The Iron Heel was first published in 1908.
